what: An upgrade of a real installation from v0.5.6 to v0.6.0, on the Windows machine this project is developed on, with a real Codex installation present
how: scripts/bootstrap.ps1 with no switches - the path a plugin at the new version takes on an ordinary setup run. It resolved the target version, downloaded the published archive, verified it against the digest pinned in the plugin, checked the archive's contents, and ran install/install.ps1.

observed_during.digest_check: SHA-256 matched the digest pinned in the plugin, not the published sidecar - the strong path, because this version was pinned before the upgrade ran

after.auto_resume: enabled, since 2026-09-10 - unchanged, so the setting survived the upgrade
after.dashboard: opened from the installed copy; Overview reports the watcher running, the engine verified, a check 22 seconds earlier, and v0.6.0

what_this_does_not_show: The watcher handover was not exercised. No watcher was running before the upgrade, so the installer started one rather than replacing one, and the check that compares a watcher's start time across an upgrade has still never seen a real restart.

No interruption happened. Nothing here shows a recovery being detected, waited out, continued or verified - this is the install-and-upgrade part of docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md and none of the parts that need a real usage limit.
Nobody watched Codex itself. The Dashboard was read and photographed; no row anywhere claims REAL CODEX VISUALLY TESTED on the strength of this.
One machine, one upgrade, from one version. v0.5.7 to v0.6.0 has not been run, and neither has a repair or an uninstall of the upgraded copy.
